h: The Fiery Serpent Awakens Teshuvah Through Divine Mercy

p: is not the Name Havayah, blessed be He,
So how is it used in connection with punishment,
מַה שֶּׁכָּתַב אַחַר כָּךְ (שָׁם כא, ח)
This fits only with the trumpets,
which is expounded: "for yourself you make,"
as it says (Midrash Rabbah and Tanchuma, Beha'alosecha);
אֲבָל כָּאן מַה הוּא לְשׁוֹן לְךָ
but here, what is the expression "for yourself"?
כִּי אֶת אֲשֶׁר יֶאֱהַב ה׳ יוֹכִיחַ
like a father the son he favors."
And so in all the rebukes in Parashas Savo
it is also written with the Name Havayah,
for in truth they are for complete mercy,
And in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 47a)
it is not written "the burning" or "the burnt,"
וְאִיתָא בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג רלא, א)
and it is brought in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 231a):
the first judgment of all is this:
who it is that does not honor
the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He,
and does not honor the Torah and His servants."
"And the Satan too came among them"
דְּאִיהוּ חָיֵישׁ נַמִּי לִיקָרָא דִּשְׁמָא דָּא
for he too is concerned for the honor of this Name
(as it says in the holy Zohar there).
וַיְשַׁלַּח ה׳ בָּעָם אֵת הַנְּחָשִׁים הַשְּׂרָפִים
"And Hashem sent against the people the fiery serpents,"
כְּדָבָר אַחֵר שְׂרָפִים עוֹמְדִים מִמַּעַל לוֹ
as it says elsewhere, "Serafim stood above Him":
that they should exact punishment for their not honoring
the Name of Hashem and His servant Moshe;
and consequently "the Satan too came among them."
And this is why it says "the serpents,"
the serpent, the woman of harlotry
(and see there in the holy Zohar);
just as it says "the Satan too"
to include that female counterpart of his.
And not as some explained the serafim
That is, Hashem Yisbarach sent angels
who exact punishment from those who are lax
and in the honor of His prophets;
And this is why it says, "Make for yourself a seraf,"
and it uses the expression "make for yourself"
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כט, א)
along the lines of what they said (Rosh Hashanah 29a):
as long as Yisrael would look
to their Father in Heaven, etc."
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁעַל יְדֵי יָדָיו שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה
That is, through the hands of Moshe,
he would instill in the hearts of Yisrael
And after this we learn in the Mishnah:
And this too is as mentioned above:
so that through it would be instilled
thoughts of teshuvah in the hearts of Yisrael.
And this is why it says, "Make for yourself a seraf":
and put his own power into it,
"he will look at it and live."

paragraphs.text: Source: Bamidbar Rabbah 15:15 — “… עשה לך, משלך. עשה לך, לך אתה עושה ולא לאחר, אתה משתמש בהן ואין אחר משתמש בהן, תדע לך שהרי יהושע תלמידו של משה לא נשתמש בהן אלא בשופרות, כשבא …” — ““Craft for you” – from your own. “Craft for you” – for yourself you craft, but not for another. You use them, but another does not use them. Know that Joshua, Moses’s disciple, did not use them, but rather shofars. …”
